outline.chapter_title: Procedural Posture and Standards of Review
outline.description: This chapter establishes the foundational procedural context of the case, explaining how the lawsuit progressed from filing to dismissal and defining the appellate court's scope of review. It clarifies why the court is limited to the allegations in the complaint and specific incorporated documents.
subtopics: Origins of the Dispute: The 'Will Santos Say It?' Segments
De Novo Review Standard for Motions to Dismiss
Scope of Evidence: Complaint Allegations, Exhibits, and Judicial Notice of Copyright Registrations

outline.chapter_title: Copyright Infringement and the Fair Use Defense
outline.description: This chapter provides a deep dive into the core legal battle: whether Kimmel's use of Santos's videos constitutes fair use. It breaks down the four statutory factors, with a heavy emphasis on the 'transformative' nature of the use and how subjective intent differs from objective perception in copyright analysis.
subtopics: The Four Statutory Factors of Fair Use (17 U.S.C. § 107)
Factor One: Transformative Purpose vs. Original Intent
The Objective Observer Test: Distinguishing Creator Intent from Secondary Use
Addressing Bad Faith Arguments: The Evolution of the *Harper & Row* Good Faith Requirement
Factors Two Through Four: Nature of Work, Amount Used, and Market Harm in Parody Contexts
Resolving Fair Use at the Pleading Stage

outline.chapter_title: Preemption and State Law Contract Claims
outline.description: This chapter analyzes Santos's alternative theories based on state contract law. It explains the concept of federal preemption under the Copyright Act but focuses primarily on why these claims failed independently due to strict requirements regarding third-party beneficiaries and the pleading of essential contract terms.
subtopics: Direct Breach of Contract: Third-Party Beneficiary Status under Illinois Law
The Presumption Against Non-Contracting Party Benefits
Implied-in-Fact Contracts: Requirements for Meeting of Minds and Essential Terms under New York Law
Failure to Plausible Allege Contract Formation via Platform Terms of Service

outline.description: This chapter isolates the specific tort claim of fraudulent inducement. It details the distinct elements required to sustain such a claim under New York law, specifically focusing on the necessity of alleging actual out-of-pocket financial loss rather than just reputational harm or hypothetical damages.
subtopics: Elements of Fraudulent Inducement under New York Common Law
The Out-of-Pocket Loss Requirement (*Lama Holding Co.*)
Distinguishing Economic Loss from Other Forms of Injury in Fraud Cases
Application to Facts: Why Payment Received Negates a Fraud Claim in This Context
